sanskrit: atra gāthā purā gītā rasātalanivāsibhiḥ paurāṇī śrūyate loke gīyate yā manīṣibhiḥ
english: Here an ancient song was sung by the dwellers of the nether world — that primordial verse which is heard and sung in the world by the wise.

sanskrit: na nāgaloke na svarge na vimāne triviṣṭape parivāsaḥ sukhas tādṛg rasātalatale yathā
english: Neither in the serpent world, nor in heaven, nor in the celestial chariot of Triviṣṭapa is there dwelling as pleasant as on the floor of Rasātala.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca iyaṃ bhogavatī nāma purī vāsukipālitā yādṛśī devarājasya purīvaryāmarāvatī
english: Nārada said: This city named Bhogavatī, guarded by Vāsuki, is like the foremost city of the king of gods — Amarāvatī.

sanskrit: eṣa śeṣaḥ sthito nāgo yeneyaṃ dhāryate sadā tapasā lokamukhyena prabhāvamahatā mahī
english: This serpent Śeṣa stands here — he by whose great tapas and immense power this earth is ever upheld, he who is foremost in all the worlds.

sanskrit: śvetoccayanibhākāro nānāvidhavibhūṣaṇaḥ sahasraṃ dhārayan mūrdhnāṃ jvālājihvo mahābalaḥ
english: Resembling a great white heap, adorned with ornaments of every kind, bearing a thousand heads, flame-tongued and of immense strength.

sanskrit: iha nānāvidhākārā nānāvidhavibhūṣaṇāḥ surasāyāḥ sutā nāgā nivasanti gatavyathāḥ
english: Here dwell the sons of Surasā — serpents of various forms and diverse ornaments — free from all distress.

sanskrit: maṇisvastikacakrāṅkāḥ kamaṇḍalukalakṛtāḥ sahasrasaṃkhyā balinaḥ sarve raudrāḥ svabhāvataḥ
english: Marked with signs of jewel, svastika, and wheel, bearing the marks of the water-vessel — thousands in number, all powerful, and fierce by nature.

sanskrit: sahasraśirasaḥ ke cit ke cit pañcaśatānanāḥ śataśīrṣās tathā ke cit ke cit triśiraso 'pi ca
english: Some bear a thousand heads, some five hundred mouths, some a hundred heads, and some even three heads.

sanskrit: dvipañcaśirasaḥ ke cit ke cit saptamukhās tathā mahābhogā mahākāyāḥ parvatābhogabhoginaḥ
english: Some have ten heads, some seven mouths; of vast coils and gigantic bodies, they are serpents whose coils rival mountains.

sanskrit: bahūnīha sahasrāṇi prayutāny arbudāni ca nāgānām ekavaṃśānāṃ yathāśreṣṭhāṃs tu me śṛṇu
english: Here dwell many thousands, millions, and hundreds of millions of serpents of a single lineage — hear from me of the most eminent among them.

sanskrit: vāsukis takṣakaś caiva karkoṭakadhanaṃjayau kālīyo nahuṣaś caiva kambalāśvatarāv ubhau
english: Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Karkoṭaka, Dhanaṃjaya, Kālīya, Nahuṣa, and both Kambala and Aśvatara —

sanskrit: bāhyakuṇḍo maṇir nāgas tathaivāpūraṇaḥ khagaḥ vāmanaś cailapatraś ca kukuraḥ kukuṇas tathā
english: Bāhyakuṇḍa, the serpent Maṇi, Āpūraṇa, Khaga, Vāmana, Elapatra, Kukura, and Kukuṇa —

sanskrit: āryako nandakaś caiva tathā kalaśapotakau kailāsakaḥ piñjarako nāgaś cairāvatas tathā
english: Āryaka, Nandaka, Kalaśa and Potaka, Kailāsaka, the serpent Piñjaraka, and Airāvata —

sanskrit: sumanomukho dadhimukhaḥ śaṅkho nandopanandakau āptaḥ koṭanakaś caiva śikhī niṣṭhūrikas tathā
english: Sumanomukha, Dadhimukha, Śaṅkha, Nanda and Upananda, Āpta, Koṭanaka, Śikhī, and Niṣṭhūrika —

sanskrit: tittirir hastibhadraś ca kumudo mālyapiṇḍakaḥ dvau padmau puṇḍarīkaś ca puṣpo mudgaraparṇakaḥ
english: Tittiri, Hastibhadra, Kumuda, Mālyapiṇḍaka, the two Padmas, Puṇḍarīka, Puṣpa, and Mudgaraparṇaka —

sanskrit: karavīraḥ pīṭharakaḥ saṃvṛtto vṛtta eva ca piṇḍāro bilvapatraś ca mūṣikādaḥ śirīṣakaḥ
english: Karavīra, Pīṭharaka, Saṃvṛtta, Vṛtta, Piṇḍāra, Bilvapatra, Mūṣikāda, and Śirīṣaka —

sanskrit: dilīpaḥ śaṅkhaśīrṣaś ca jyotiṣko 'thāparājitaḥ kauravyo dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca kumāraḥ kuśakas tathā
english: Dilīpa, Śaṅkhaśīrṣa, Jyotiṣka, and Aparājita, Kauravya, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Kumāra, and Kuśaka —

sanskrit: virajā dhāraṇaś caiva subāhur mukharo jayaḥ badhirāndhau vikuṇḍaś ca virasaḥ surasas tathā
english: Virajā, Dhāraṇa, Subāhu, Mukhara, Jaya, Badhira, Andha, Vikuṇḍa, Virasa, and Surasā —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ kaśyapasyātmajāḥ smṛtāḥ mātale paśya yady atra kaś cit te rocate varaḥ
english: These and many others are remembered as the sons of Kaśyapa. Mātali, look — if any among them pleases you as a suitable choice.

sanskrit: kaṇva uvāca mātalis tv ekam avyagraḥ satataṃ saṃnirīkṣya vai papraccha nāradaṃ tatra prītimān iva cābhavat
english: Kaṇva said: Mātali, calm and intent, having gazed steadily at one of them, questioned Nārada there, appearing as one filled with affection.

sanskrit: sthito ya eṣa purataḥ kauravyasyāryakasya ca dyutimān darśanīyaś ca kasyaiṣa kulanandanaḥ
english: "Who is this one standing before Kauravya and Āryaka — so radiant and handsome? Whose son is this, the joy of what lineage?"

sanskrit: kaḥ pitā jananī cāsya katamasyaiṣa bhoginaḥ vaṃśasya kasyaiṣa mahān ketubhūta iva sthitaḥ
english: "Who is his father, who his mother? Of which serpent family does he belong? Whose lineage does this great one stand as a banner?"

sanskrit: praṇidhānena dhairyeṇa rūpeṇa vayasā ca me manaḥ praviṣṭo devarṣe guṇakeśyāḥ patir varaḥ
english: "By his self-possession, steadiness, beauty, and youth, O divine sage, he has entered my mind — he seems a worthy husband for Guṇakeśī."

sanskrit: mātaliṃ prītimanasaṃ dṛṣṭvā sumukhadarśanāt nivedayām āsa tadā māhātmyaṃ janma karma ca
english: Seeing Mātali pleased at the sight of Sumukha, Nārada then described his greatness, birth, and deeds.

sanskrit: airāvatakule jātaḥ sumukho nāma nāgarāṭ āryakasya mataḥ pautro dauhitro vāmanasya ca
english: "Born in the lineage of Airāvata, this serpent-prince is named Sumukha — regarded as the grandson of Āryaka and the daughter's son of Vāmana."

sanskrit: etasya hi pitā nāgaś cikuro nāma mātale nacirād vainateyena pañcatvam upapāditaḥ
english: "The father of this serpent, named Cikura, O Mātali, was not long ago reduced to the five elements by Vainateya."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt prītamanā mātalir nāradaṃ vacaḥ eṣa me rucitas tāta jāmātā bhujagottamaḥ
english: Then, with a pleased mind, Mātali said to Nārada: "This foremost of serpents is agreeable to me, dear friend, as a son-in-law."

sanskrit: kriyatām atra yatno hi prītimān asmy anena vai asya nāgapater dātuṃ priyāṃ duhitaraṃ mune
english: "Let effort be made in this matter — I am delighted with him. To give this lord of serpents my beloved daughter in marriage, O sage."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca sūto 'yaṃ mātalir nāma śakrasya dayitaḥ suhṛt śuciḥ śīlaguṇopetas tejasvī vīryavān balī
english: Nārada said: "This charioteer named Mātali is the beloved and trusted friend of Śakra — pure, endowed with good character and virtue, resplendent, valiant, and strong."

sanskrit: śakrasyāyaṃ sakhā caiva mantrī sārathir eva ca alpāntaraprabhāvaś ca vāsavena raṇe raṇe
english: "He is the companion, counselor, and charioteer of Śakra, hardly differing in power from Vāsava in battle after battle."

sanskrit: ayaṃ harisahasreṇa yuktaṃ jaitraṃ rathottamam devāsureṣu yuddheṣu manasaiva niyacchati
english: "In the wars between gods and demons, he controls by mere thought alone the victorious foremost chariot yoked to a thousand tawny horses."

sanskrit: anena vijitān aśvair dorbhyāṃ jayati vāsavaḥ anena prahṛte pūrvaṃ balabhit praharaty uta
english: "Through him, Vāsava wins with his horses and arms those who are conquered; when this one strikes first, then Balabhit strikes."

sanskrit: asya kanyā varārohā rūpeṇāsadṛśī bhuvi sattvaśīlaguṇopetā guṇakeśīti viśrutā
english: "His daughter, of noble bearing, has no equal on earth in beauty; endowed with virtue, character, and quality — she is known as Guṇakeśī."

sanskrit: tasyāsya yatnāc caratas trailokyam amaradyute sumukho bhavataḥ pautro rocate duhituḥ patiḥ
english: "While this one searches the three worlds with effort, O resplendent among the immortals, your grandson Sumukha pleases him as a husband for his daughter."

sanskrit: yadi te rocate saumya bhujagottama māciram kriyatām āryaka kṣipraṃ buddhiḥ kanyāpratigrahe
english: "If this pleases you, O gentle one, foremost of serpents, then without delay, O Āryaka, quickly form a decision to accept the girl."

sanskrit: yathā viṣṇukule lakṣmīr yathā svāhā vibhāvasoḥ kule tava tathaivāstu guṇakeśī sumadhyamā
english: "As Lakṣmī is in Viṣṇu's lineage, as Svāhā is in the lineage of Vibhāvasu — so let Guṇakeśī of the lovely waist be in your family."

sanskrit: pautrasyārthe bhavāṃs tasmād guṇakeśīṃ pratīcchatu sadṛśīṃ pratirūpasya vāsavasya śacīm iva
english: "For the sake of your grandson, therefore let your honor accept Guṇakeśī — she who is comparable in beauty to Śacī herself, fitting consort of Vāsava."

sanskrit: pitṛhīnam api hy enaṃ guṇato varayāmahe bahumānāc ca bhavatas tathaivairāvatasya ca sumukhasya guṇaiś caiva śīlaśaucadamādibhiḥ
english: "Even though fatherless, we choose him for his qualities — out of great respect for your honor, for Airāvata, and for Sumukha's own qualities of good conduct, purity, and self-restraint."

sanskrit: abhigamya svayaṃ kanyām ayaṃ dātuṃ samudyataḥ mātales tasya saṃmānaṃ kartum arho bhavān api
english: "Having approached of his own accord, Mātali stands ready to give his daughter; you too, O Āryaka, should honor him in return."

sanskrit: kaṇva uvāca sa tu dīnaḥ prahṛṣṭaś ca prāha nāradam āryakaḥ vriyamāṇe tathā pautre putre ca nidhanaṃ gate
english: Kaṇva said: Āryaka, both sorrowful and joyful at once, spoke to Nārada — his grandson now being sought in marriage, while his own son had gone to death.

sanskrit: na me naitad bahumataṃ devarṣe vacanaṃ tava sakhā śakrasya saṃyuktaḥ kasyāyaṃ nepsito bhavet
english: "O divine sage, who would not desire this? Your word is highly esteemed by me — he who is connected to Śakra's own companion, who would not welcome this?"

sanskrit: kāraṇasya tu daurbalyāc cintayāmi mahāmune asya dehakaras tāta mama putro mahādyute bhakṣito vainateyena duḥkhārtās tena vai vayam
english: "But because of the weakness of our situation I reflect, O great sage — the progenitor of this one, O dear, my son was devoured by Vainateya, O greatly resplendent one; we are afflicted with that grief."

sanskrit: punar eva ca tenoktaṃ vainateyena gacchatā māsenānyena sumukhaṃ bhakṣayiṣya iti prabho
english: "And again, as Vainateya departed, he declared: within another month I shall devour Sumukha, O lord."

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ tathā tad bhavitā jānīmas tasya niścayam tena harṣaḥ pranaṣṭo me suparṇavacanena vai
english: "That shall certainly come to pass — we know his resolve. Thus my joy is destroyed by the words of Suparṇa."

sanskrit: mātalis tv abravīd enaṃ buddhir atra kṛtā mayā jāmātṛbhāvena vṛtaḥ sumukhas tava putrajaḥ
english: Mātali then said to him: "My mind is resolved in this matter. Sumukha, the son of your son, has been chosen by me as a son-in-law."

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ mayā ca sahito nāradena ca pannagaḥ trilokeśaṃ surapatiṃ gatvā paśyatu vāsavam
english: "Let this serpent accompanied by me and by Nārada go to see Vāsava, the lord of the gods, the ruler of the three worlds."

sanskrit: śeṣeṇaivāsya kāryeṇa prajñāsyāmy aham āyuṣaḥ suparṇasya vighāte ca prayatiṣyāmi sattama
english: "Through the remaining matter of his life I shall provide wisdom, O best of beings, and I shall strive to thwart Suparṇa."

sanskrit: sumukhaś ca mayā sārdhaṃ deveśam abhigacchatu kāryasaṃsādhanārthāya svasti te 'stu bhujaṃgama
english: "And let Sumukha accompany me to the lord of gods, for the accomplishment of this purpose. May all be well with you, O serpent."

sanskrit: tatas te sumukhaṃ gṛhya sarva eva mahaujasaḥ dadṛśuḥ śakram āsīnaṃ devarājaṃ mahādyutim
english: Then all those mighty ones, taking Sumukha with them, beheld Śakra seated — the king of gods, of great splendor.

sanskrit: saṃgatyā tatra bhagavān viṣṇur āsīc caturbhujaḥ tatas tat sarvam ācakhyau nārado mātaliṃ prati
english: By chance the blessed Viṣṇu of four arms was present there; and then Nārada recounted everything to Mātali.

sanskrit: tataḥ puraṃdaraṃ viṣṇur uvāca bhuvaneśvaram amṛtaṃ dīyatām asmai kriyatām amaraiḥ samaḥ
english: Then Viṣṇu spoke to Puraṃdara, lord of the worlds: "Let amṛta be given to him; let him be made equal to the immortals."

sanskrit: mātalir nāradaś caiva sumukhaś caiva vāsava labhantāṃ bhavataḥ kāmāt kāmam etaṃ yathepsitam
english: "Let Mātali, Nārada, and Sumukha obtain this wished-for boon, O Vāsava, through your grace, as each desires."

sanskrit: puraṃdaro 'tha saṃcintya vainateyaparākramam viṣṇum evābravīd enaṃ bhavān eva dadātv iti
english: Puraṃdara then, reflecting on the prowess of Vainateya, said to Viṣṇu himself: "Let your honor bestow it."

sanskrit: viṣṇur uvāca īśas tvam asi lokānāṃ carāṇām acarāś ca ye tvayā dattam adattaṃ kaḥ kartum utsahate vibho
english: Viṣṇu said: "You are the lord of all the worlds — of those that move and those that do not. What you give or withhold, O mighty one, who dares to undo?"

sanskrit: kaṇva uvāca prādāc chakras tatas tasmai pannagāyāyur uttamam na tv enam amṛtaprāśaṃ cakāra balavṛtrahā
english: Kaṇva said: Then Śakra bestowed upon that serpent the highest span of life; yet Balavṛtrahā did not make him partake of the amṛta.

sanskrit: labdhvā varaṃ tu sumukhaḥ sumukhaḥ saṃbabhūva ha kṛtadāro yathākāmaṃ jagāma ca gṛhān prati
english: Having received the boon, Sumukha became truly Sumukha — of beautiful countenance; he took a wife as he wished and returned to his home.

sanskrit: nāradas tv āryakaś caiva kṛtakāryau mudā yutau pratijagmatur abhyarcya devarājaṃ mahādyutim
english: Nārada and Āryaka, their purpose accomplished, filled with joy, returned after honoring the great-splendored king of gods.

sanskrit: kaṇva uvāca garuḍas tat tu śuśrāva yathāvṛttaṃ mahābalaḥ āyuḥpradānaṃ śakreṇa kṛtaṃ nāgasya bhārata
english: Kaṇva said: Garuḍa, of immense power, heard what had transpired — the grant of long life bestowed on the serpent by Śakra, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pakṣavātena mahatā ruddhvā tribhuvanaṃ khagaḥ suparṇaḥ paramakruddho vāsavaṃ samupādravat
english: Blocking the three worlds with the mighty wind of his wings, that bird Suparṇa, supremely enraged, rushed toward Vāsava.

sanskrit: garuḍa uvāca bhagavan kim avajñānāt kṣudhāṃ prati bhaye mama kāmakāravaraṃ dattvā punaś calitavān asi
english: Garuḍa said: "O lord, out of disregard, have you given away freely a boon concerning my food, and thus moved against me while I was in need? Have you abandoned our agreement?"

sanskrit: nisargāt sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvabhūteśvareṇa me āhāro vihito dhātrā kimarthaṃ vāryate tvayā
english: "By nature, the ordainer who is lord of all beings ordained food for me — why then is it being withheld by you?"

sanskrit: vṛtaś caiṣa mahānāgaḥ sthāpitaḥ samayaś ca me anena ca mayā deva bhartavyaḥ prasavo mahān
english: "This great serpent was claimed, an agreement was established by me; and through this one, O god, a great multitude of dependents must be supported by me."

sanskrit: etasmiṃs tv anyathābhūte nānyaṃ hiṃsitum utsahe krīḍase kāmakāreṇa devarāja yathecchakam
english: "With this one denied to me, I would not venture to harm another; yet you sport capriciously, O king of gods, entirely as you please."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ prāṇān vimokṣyāmi tathā parijano mama ye ca bhṛtyā mama gṛhe prītimān bhava vāsava
english: "Thus I shall relinquish my life, and so too will my retinue and the servants in my household. Be pleased, O Vāsava."

sanskrit: etac caivāham arhāmi bhūyaś ca balavṛtrahan trailokyasyeśvaro yo 'haṃ parabhṛtyatvam āgataḥ
english: "This and more I deserve, O slayer of Bala and Vṛtra — I who am lord of the three worlds have been reduced to servitude under another."

sanskrit: tvayi tiṣṭhati deveśa na viṣṇuḥ kāraṇaṃ mama trailokyarāja rājyaṃ hi tvayi vāsava śāśvatam
english: "With you standing here, O lord of gods, Viṣṇu is not the cause of my grievance — for the sovereignty of the three worlds, O Vāsava, rests eternally with you."

sanskrit: mamāpi dakṣasya sutā jananī kaśyapaḥ pitā aham apy utsahe lokān samastān voḍhum añjasā
english: "My mother too is the daughter of Dakṣa, Kaśyapa is my father; I too am capable of bearing all the worlds with ease."

sanskrit: asahyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ mamāpi vipulaṃ balam mayāpi sumahat karma kṛtaṃ daiteyavigrahe
english: "My immense power too is unbearable by all beings; great deeds were performed by me as well in the battle against the Daityas."

sanskrit: śrutaśrīḥ śrutasenaś ca vivasvān rocanāmukhaḥ prasabhaḥ kālakākṣaś ca mayāpi ditijā hatāḥ
english: "Śrutaśrī, Śrutasena, Vivasvān, Rocanāmukha, Prasabha, and Kālakākṣa — these sons of Diti were also slain by me."

sanskrit: yat tu dhvajasthānagato yatnāt paricarāmy aham vahāmi caivānujaṃ te tena mām avamanyase
english: "But because I serve diligently, stationed as your emblem on the flagstaff, and carry your younger brother — on that account you disrespect me."

sanskrit: ko 'nyo bhārasaho hy asti ko 'nyo 'sti balavattaraḥ mayā yo 'haṃ viśiṣṭaḥ san vahāmīmaṃ sabāndhavam
english: "Who else can bear such a burden? Who else is mightier than I — I who, though superior, carry him along with his kin?"

sanskrit: avajñāya tu yat te 'haṃ bhojanād vyaparopitaḥ tena me gauravaṃ naṣṭaṃ tvattaś cāsmāc ca vāsava
english: "Because I have been deprived of my food out of disregard for me, my honor is destroyed — both before you and before the others, O Vāsava."

sanskrit: adityāṃ ya ime jātā balavikramaśālinaḥ tvam eṣāṃ kila sarveṣāṃ viśeṣād balavattaraḥ
english: "Those born of Aditi who are endowed with strength and valor — among all of them it is said that you are especially the mightiest."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ pakṣaikadeśena vahāmi tvāṃ gataklamaḥ vimṛśa tvaṃ śanais tāta ko nv atra balavān iti
english: "Yet I carry you with just a portion of one wing, without exertion. Reflect slowly, dear one — who then is truly powerful here?"

sanskrit: kaṇva uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā khagasyodarkadāruṇam akṣobhyaṃ kṣobhayaṃs tārkṣyam uvāca rathacakrabhṛt
english: Kaṇva said: Hearing those words of the bird — terrible in their consequences — he who bears the wheel on his chariot, though unshakeable, spoke agitating Tārkṣya.

sanskrit: garutman manyase ''tmānaṃ balavantaṃ sudurbalam alam asmatsamakṣaṃ te stotum ātmānam aṇḍaja
english: "O Garutman, you think yourself powerful — you are utterly weak. Enough of this self-praise before us, O egg-born one."

sanskrit: trailokyam api me kṛtsnam aśaktaṃ dehadhāraṇe aham evātmanātmānaṃ vahāmi tvāṃ ca dhāraye
english: "The entire three worlds are unable to bear my body; I sustain even myself by my own power — and I also uphold you."

sanskrit: imaṃ tāvan mamaikaṃ tvaṃ bāhuṃ savyetaraṃ vaha yady enaṃ dhārayasy ekaṃ saphalaṃ te vikatthitam
english: "Bear then just this one arm of mine — the right one; if you can hold even that single one, then your boasting shall have borne fruit."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavāṃs tasya skandhe bāhuṃ samāsajat nipapāta sa bhārārto vihvalo naṣṭacetanaḥ
english: Then the blessed one placed his arm upon Garuḍa's shoulder — and he fell, crushed by the weight, overwhelmed and bereft of consciousness.

sanskrit: yāvān hi bhāraḥ kṛtsnāyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ parvataiḥ saha ekasyā dehaśākhāyās tāvad bhāram amanyata
english: For he felt a weight equal to that of the entire earth together with its mountains — all pressing upon that single limb of his body.
